title: Planning Ahead: Understanding Bank Holidays from June 25 to 28
description: Indian banks will observe regional holidays and weekends, leading to closures for up to four days between June 25 and June 28, 2026. These closures are state-.

faq.q: How do I know if my bank is closed in my city?
faq.a: You should check the official holiday calendar published by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on its website (rbi.org.in). These calendars specify state-wise bank holidays under the Negotiable Instruments Act.

faq.q: Will online transactions like UPI and IMPS work during bank holidays?
faq.a: Yes, digital payment systems such as UPI (Unified Payments Interface) and IMPS (Immediate Payment Service) operate 24x7, 365 days a year, including bank holidays. You can use them for instant fund transfers.

faq.q: What about NEFT and RTGS during bank holidays?
faq.a: NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer) and RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement) also operate 24x7. While you can initiate these transactions, the final crediting to the beneficiary account might experience slight delays if the receiving bank's internal processing is tied to working hours.

faq.q: Can I withdraw cash from ATMs during bank holidays?
faq.a: Yes, ATMs will be operational for cash withdrawals and other services during bank holidays. However, it's advisable to plan your cash needs in advance, as some ATMs might temporarily run out of cash due to higher demand during extended closures.

faq.q: What happens if my cheque clearing date falls on a bank holiday?
faq.a: If your cheque clearing date falls on a bank holiday, the cheque will typically be processed on the next immediate working day. This means the funds will be credited to your account with a corresponding delay.

faq.q: Will my EMI or bill payments be affected if due on a bank holiday?
faq.a: If you have set up automatic debits (NACH mandates) for EMIs or bill payments, they might be processed on the next working day. However, it's always best to ensure sufficient funds are available in your account a day before the holiday to avoid any missed payments or charges.

faq.q: Where can I find the official RBI holiday calendar?
faq.a: The official RBI holiday calendar is available on the Reserve Bank of India's website, rbi.org.in, usually under the "Notifications" or "Press Releases" section, or by searching for "Bank Holidays."
